title: 2008 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement: Rectangle \(PQRS\) lies in a plane with \(PQ = RS = 2\) and \(QR = SP = 6.\) The rectangle is rotated \(90^\circ\) clockwise about \(R,\) then rotated \(90^\circ\) clockwise about the point that \(S\) moved to after the first rotation. What is the length of the path traveled by point \(P?\)

solutions.text:
In the first rotation, \(P\) moves on a quarter circle about \(R\) with radius \(PR = \sqrt{2^2 + 6^2} = 2\sqrt{10}.\) The arc length is \(\dfrac{1}{4}\left(2\pi \cdot 2\sqrt{10}\right) = \sqrt{10}\,\pi.\)

In the second rotation, \(P\) moves on a quarter circle about the new position of \(S\) with radius \(6.\) The arc length is \(\dfrac{1}{4}(2\pi \cdot 6) = 3\pi.\)

The total path length is \(\left(3 + \sqrt{10}\right)\pi.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Point \(P\) traces one quarter-circle arc for each rotation
The first radius is \(PR = \sqrt{40};\) the second radius is the side of length \(6\)
